subject: Post-call: Model fit & prompt collection for Acme - next steps
body_preview: Recap of discovery call, recommended models and request for customer prompt set + redaction guidance.
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-20T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call: Model fit & prompt collection for Acme - next steps

Hi Alex — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

Recap
- Goal: reduce manual triage time for incoming customer support tickets and surface suggested replies with high precision.
- Data: ~150k tickets/year, median ticket length ~250 tokens, peak latency target <300ms for first token at 95th pctl.
- Constraints: PII redaction required, SOC 2 in progress, prefer self-hosted/private deployment for regulated customers.

Recommended short list for model fit evaluation
- rwd-7b-quant (fast, lower cost) — good baseline for throughput testing
- rwd-13b-ptq (balanced quality/cost) — recommended for initial evals
- rwd-70b-llm-fp16 (higher quality, higher cost) — for accuracy-sensitive spend

Next steps (ask to Alex)
1) Please share a representative prompt set (sanitized) including edge cases (escalations, legal requests, embedded code blocks). We typically ask for 200–500 prompts across categories.
2) Add a short label column for "expected intent" and "safety_risk" (low/medium/high) if possible.
3) If you have existing evaluations or benchmark links, attach those.

I've attached a prompt collection template to make the export easier. If you need guidance on redaction, see the section below.

Redaction guidance (quick)
- Replace direct PII (names, emails, phone numbers, exact account IDs) with consistent tokens: [NAME], [EMAIL], [PHONE], [ACCOUNT_ID].
- Keep enough context for intent (do not remove entire quoted thread).
- For occasionally sensitive fields (payment info, SSNs), replace with [REDACTED_SENSITIVE].

I can run a quick smoke eval once you share the file and then we can schedule a 30-min sync to review results and pick the model to run a full benchmark.

Thanks —
Marissa
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0199
[attachment: prompt_collection_template.csv (text/csv)]

Date: 2026-02-21T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Model fit & prompt collection for Acme - next steps

Hi Marissa — thanks for the summary, this is helpful. Attaching a first pass export of ~250 prompts from our support queue. We redacted obvious PII but left contextual placeholders. See attached CSV.

A few notes from our side:
- We have a separate folder with escalation examples (legal, regulatory) that I can share if useful.
- Security asked for confirmation on whether sample prompts can include hashed account IDs (we'd prefer to keep hashing instead of [ACCOUNT_ID] placeholders). Is that acceptable?

Attaching: acme_sample_prompts.csv

Thanks,
Alex Johnson

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-23T09:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Model fit & prompt collection for Acme - next steps

Thanks Alex — got the file and appreciate the hashing note. Quick answers and a proposed evaluation plan: 

Hashing vs placeholders
- Hashed account IDs are fine for model-fit and latency tests as long as the hashing is consistent across prompts (we only need to detect patterns, not map to real accounts). For safety/regression checks we prefer placeholders but we can work with hashed values for initial runs.

Evaluation plan (proposed)
1) Smoke run: 200 prompts through rwd-7b-quant and rwd-13b-ptq to get latency, token cost, and quick quality signals (we can do this within 48 hours once you confirm).
2) If quality baseline looks good on rwd-13b-ptq, run a 1k prompt benchmark across rwd-13b-ptq and rwd-70b-llm-fp16 (accuracy + safety/regression checks).
3) We'll produce a short report with precision@top1 for suggested replies, common failure modes, and any safety flags.

Prompt template/labels
- Thanks for using the template — two small asks to help with automated evals:
  - Add an "expected_reply" column where possible (a short human-written exemplar reply).
  - Add tags for edge cases: code_block, legal_escalation, pii_leak_risk.

Redaction checklist (attached as inline guidance):
- OK to keep consistent hashed IDs.
- Remove/replace free-text payment identifiers with [REDACTED_SENSITIVE].
- Keep quoted conversation context but remove inline email addresses.

Next steps
- Can you confirm: are you able to add the expected_reply column and the 3 tags? If not, still send what you have — we can annotate a 200-sample subset for the smoke run.
- Once you confirm, I'll queue the smoke eval and share a short observation deck + benchmark link.

Sample benchmarks and resources:
- Benchmark report (example): https://redwood-inference.com/benchmarks/support-assist-2025
- Model card overview: https://redwood-inference.com/models/rwd-13b-ptq

Cheers,
Marissa
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
